known_issues: Undisclosed adapter fields and hook names: suites use `S.HookPrefix`, `S.TimerName` and the suffixes `.Death`/`.Spawn`/`.Disconnect`/`.Removed` (benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/integration/hot-object-round-controller-integration.lua:4,6,9,10,11,13; benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/server/hot-object-round-controller-suite.lua clean(): `server.TimerName`, `server.HookPrefix .. ".Death"`). The exam (T4-NATIVE-01) requires named hooks and a timer but publishes no name or field. Measured by control alternative-strict-reading.

Private snapshot/save layout: player state is read as `snapshot.players.<ID>` or `snapshot.player_rows[i]`, and events as `seen` or `event_rows` (benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/hidden/hot-object-round-controller.lua:10,16; benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/server/hot-object-round-controller-suite.lua Phase A `variants`/`lifecycle` checks). T4-PERSIST-01 asks for all player state with stably sorted lists; a sorted `players` LIST, a natural reading, makes `s.players.B` nil and errors. Measured by control alternative-strict-reading-layout (only the list keys renamed to `players`/`events`): it fails the hidden infectious and malformed-state cases, and Phase A never emits a result (the suite indexes `players.B` on a list), leaving all eight server cases unobserved (55.71).

Undisclosed Dispatch event shape `{kind="touch", object=<Entity>, player=<Player>}` (benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/integration/hot-object-round-controller-integration.lua:8); T4-ADAPTER-01 names only kind, event_id, sequence and now. StartRound is likewise called with Player objects for `players`/`holder` (benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/integration/hot-object-round-controller-integration.lua:5; benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/server/hot-object-round-controller-suite.lua Phase A/B) although the exam does not say whether these are Players or logical IDs.

Fixture trap: the stub adapter environment has only include, hook (Add/Remove), timer (Create/Remove), IsValid and CurTime (benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/integration/hot-object-round-controller-integration.lua:2-3); stub entities are bare tables. Any other GMod global or Entity method on an exercised path errors only in this layer.

Non-discriminating native assertion: Phase A's `infectious excludes infected B from winners` (benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/server/hot-object-round-controller-suite.lua, Phase A final block) is evaluated after B has been kicked, so B is absent from winners for being disconnected whether or not infection is honoured. Control infected-survivors-can-win passes both server phases; only the hidden case detects it.
Vacuous assertion: Phase B `physical-touch` is `check(..., true)` (benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/server/hot-object-round-controller-suite.lua, Phase B branch).

Shared stub state: integration cases 2-10 run one round on one adapter in sequence (benchmarks/gmod/private/tasks/hot-object-round-controller/integration/hot-object-round-controller-integration.lua:5-13); an early defect fails later cases.

Server-layer case granularity: the five-to-eight `server:` cases are the group verdicts of the FINAL phase (B) only (plugins/garrys-mod/src/rhenium_garrys_mod/addons/evaluator.py:255-276 reads `final_payload['cases']`). A failed Phase A assertion stops the run before Phase B (server_runner.py:631-640), so it is never recorded as `F` on its group: every `server:` case becomes unobserved (`U`), `complete` is false and the dedicated-server check scores 0/40. The Phase A group verdicts do exist in the raw execution record (`result.runtime.phase_a.payload.cases`) but are not part of the case table. Phase-A-only evidence therefore acts as a gate, not as a named failing case. Here Phase A holds the real physical touch, infection, Kill/Spawn/Kick lifecycle and the infectious deadline; Phase B holds restore (audit/result/settlements), a fresh timer-driven exploding round and Shutdown residue.
